what: R56.1 cost gate (round 7 change-arrival spec 4): busy time of the top-level tasks on the renderer's compositor thread and the display compositor thread inside one warmed change from home to the portfolio page, from scripts/audit/make-glass-cost.mjs (a trace between two performance marks), headless Chrome on an M4 Pro. Gate: Renderer/Compositor at most 450 ms, GPU Process/VizCompositorThread at most 300 ms, every frame presented (no STATE_DROPPED), three runs each, all three must pass. The busy times sum top-level tasks together with the thread-controller wrapper task round each (both are `toplevel` slices), so each is about 2x the thread's self time (a DevTools profile reads about half); the verdicts hold because the baseline, the thresholds and the ratio all use the same measure.

gpu_main_thread_question.asked: in the review of R56.1: gpuMainMs (busy time of the top-level tasks on GPU Process/CrGpuMain) went from 629/584/697 (R54) to 916/851/2547 (R56.1) at 1920x1080@1, 2547 of a 2563 ms window in the third run
gpu_main_thread_question.answer: It is waiting, not work, and it is not a texture upload or a decode. make-glass-cost.mjs now names the slices behind the number (self time by name, gpuMainTop, split into waits and work as gpuMainWaitMs and gpuMainWorkMs; --gpu-detail adds the GPU service and ANGLE categories). On both builds the thread spends its time in two waits: CALayerTreeCoordinator::ApplyBackpressure::Metal (the thread blocked, polling every millisecond, until the display hands it a drawable; it grows when the display is busy or the machine is loaded: 23 to 1,669 ms in the same build) and IOSurfaceImageBacking::WaitForCommandsToBeScheduled::Dawn (waiting for the renderer compositor to have scheduled its commands; 44 to 1,585 ms, the larger on R54 whose renderer compositor is slower). What it works at is the same in both builds: SkiaOutputSurfaceImplOnGpu::FinishPaintRenderPass about 90 to 116 ms, RasterDecoderImpl::DoEndRasterCHROMIUM::Flush about 50 ms, SubmitToGPU about 80 to 96 ms, and graphite DrawAtlas::recordUploads 11 ms (the only upload slice; the 23 href swaps per filter leave no slice of their own, no image decode is on the thread). Work (self time less the waits): R56.1b 228 to 256 ms at both sizes in 6 runs; R54 173 to 283 ms in 6 runs. The toplevel sum in gpuMainMs also counts a task and the thread-controller task around it twice (the self time is half of it), which is why one run showed nearly the whole window.
gpu_main_thread_question.answer_wording_after_re_review: CrGpuMain's own work is unchanged; the rest is waiting on the display or GPU pipeline, which grows with load and is no larger than R54's in the same hour. (A CPU trace cannot tell the display's wait from the GPU running the page's own filters, and every sliced run was on a loaded machine, so the load is inferred from the variance between runs, not isolated.)
gpu_main_thread_question.so: nothing was reduced: there is no per-swap upload or decode to remove. The gate stays on the two compositor threads. A display that is busy (After Effects at 170% CPU and a WindowServer at 60% during these runs) lengthens the backpressure wait in either build; a dropped frame count above 0 together with a long ApplyBackpressure is the machine, and the gate is for a quiet one.

long_frame_133ms.asked: the 133 ms frame at 2311 ms in the first change of page-change-hook.json run 1 of R56.1: name its long-animation-frame script, or say it had none
long_frame_133ms.answer: its entry was not kept: the run was summarised to the frame gaps only and the raw output of the run was not saved, so its script cannot be named. It did not come back in 11 runs of page-change-hook.json on this build (all first changes: 10 clean, 1 with a cluster of 50 to 83 ms frames at 1154 to 1604 ms into the change). The loaf entries of that cluster, which is the same kind of frame, name the page, not the glass: MessagePort.onmessage (React scheduler, components chunk) 6 to 85 ms in a frame (the new page being rendered, up to 24 ms of it forced style and layout), page timers (_index chunk) 24 to 31 ms and FrameRequestCallback of the page-change chunk (the glass tick) 6 to 14 ms; no frame is the glass tick alone. The page-mount cost is task 28's.

The R33 gate of "no frame over 34 ms in the first change" is therefore not met in 2 of these 3 runs, on a machine under load; the same first change with the build as committed (fe51bca) in interleaved A/B runs: 2 of 4 had a slow frame (83 and 50 ms at about 260 ms), the new build 1 of 4 (50 ms at 272 ms), so the change does not make it worse.
